### This is a beta release

This build is for testing only. It is published as a pre-release, so it is not offered to
existing installations through the in-app updater — install it by hand from the assets below.

### The Windows upgrade test from beta.8 still stands

Nothing about "remove the old DisplayMux install before installing", added in beta.8, changed
here. If you have not checked it yet, install this build over an older one and confirm the same
three things:

- Apps & Features lists only DisplayMuxAuto
- The old install folder is gone
- **After a reboot only one copy is running**

### Fixes

- A failed theme sync no longer takes the whole interface with it. `getCurrentWindow()` throws
  rather than rejecting when there is no window to reach, and the theme module calls it while the
  app is still starting — so the colour of a native title bar could cost the window its contents.
  The page's own colours are already applied by that point.
- Three icons no longer render as empty squares. The two display-identity cards, and the alert on
  the note saying a change is waiting for the save button, asked for icon names that were never
  registered, so each drew a coloured box with nothing in it. The screen asking you to declare
  that two displays are one is not the place to look unfinished.
- A paired host's row no longer breaks when more than one display is shared. Each shared display
  adds its own input control, and with two of them the host's own name was squeezed into breaking
  across lines, taking its address and buttons with it. The row wraps now.
- In English the appearance control no longer reads "System appearanc".
- The product name above the host switcher window was renamed. It was written into the markup
  rather than the locales, so both earlier renames missed it.
- Two labels described behaviour the app no longer has: the hint shown when a display's inputs
  cannot be read still promised a list of common ports (there is none), and this computer's input
  was still labelled "automatically detected" (it has been editable for two releases).

### Documentation

- Both READMEs were rewritten. Their feature list stopped at v0.1.3 and was missing several
  shared displays and switching them in one action, the global host switcher, merging the
  identities one display reports in different modes, the two reset scopes, editing this
  computer's name, setting a port by hand, and what hosts now sync between themselves.
- The two stale screenshots were replaced, and three views the text describes but never showed
  were added: added hosts and reset, identity merging, and the switcher window.

### Known limitations

- Undoing a merge leaves the inputs and notes that merging folded into the display the other
  identity joined.
- Ports, merges and host names only sync between hosts running this version.
- The macOS DMG is ad-hoc signed but not notarized with an Apple Developer ID, so Gatekeeper may
  require manual approval.

### What to test

- Share two displays, then check that the "added hosts and inputs" card on the settings page
  still lays out properly.
- Make one display undetectable (change its display mode, or unplug it) and confirm the icons on
  the identity-merge cards actually draw.
